//dut: G0 smoke vehicle: aer_fifo at the EVQ geometry of docs/10 section 7.1 (16-bit event word, 64 entries). The parameters are the module defaults, but they are pinned here explicitly so the hardened geometry is a property of this config rather than of the RTL header -- the numbers in docs/12 are only meaningful against a stated WIDTH/DEPTH. Pinning them is not cosmetic: chparam-ing WIDTH and DEPTH to the values they already had changes the netlist from 4160 cells / 89266.061 um2 to 4164 cells / 89320.455 um2 (docs/12 section 4.7).
//clock: 30 ns (33 MHz), deliberately loose. The block is a register file with a pointer adder, so timing is not the experiment here -- PDK and flow integration is. An unreachable constraint manufactures thousands of phantom violations and hides the real integration failures behind them (lesson recorded by the sibling SKY130 project). Achieved slack is reported per corner in docs/12 section 4.4: 18.0553 ns setup at the slow corner, i.e. the whole path fits in 11.945 ns, so the TT-class 50 MHz envelope is measured rather than asserted here.
//setup: Without this key Checker.SetupViolations resolves its corner list as SETUP_VIOLATION_CORNERS or TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS, SETUP_VIOLATION_CORNERS has no default, and this PDK ships TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS as ['*typ*'] -- so the checker examines nom_typ_1p20V_25C and NOTHING ELSE, and nom_slow_1p08V_125C, the corner that decides whether the part works, is gated by no checker at all. docs/28 section 4.4a. HOLD_VIOLATION_CORNERS is the only one of the four that needed nothing: LibreLane itself ships it as ['*'], which trial-03-signoff's resolved.json confirms. THIS CONFIG WAS THE LAST ONE IN THE REPOSITORY STILL IN THAT STATE, and the run it left unguarded is not a minor one. trial-03-signoff/resolved.json reads SETUP_VIOLATION_CORNERS null against TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS ['*typ*'], and checker_audit.py on that run tree calls Checker.SetupViolations PARTIAL -- 'matches 1 of 3 measured corners; unchecked: nom_fast_1p32V_m40C, nom_slow_1p08V_125C'. That is the run ROADMAP gate G0 cites for '0 setup, hold, max-slew and max-cap violations across all three corners'. The per-corner metrics in that run really are 0 at all three, so the sentence is true as a MEASUREMENT; what was not true is that anything would have stopped the run had they not been. Added 2026-09-10. The G0 run is not re-run and its numbers stand as recorded (docs/64): this key binds the NEXT run of this config, not that one.
//capslew: A DIFFERENT MECHANISM FROM THE SETUP ONE, and the obvious fix is inert. Checker.MaxCapViolations and Checker.MaxSlewViolations each declare corner_override = [''] in librelane/steps/checker.py, and get_corner_variable() promotes that into the Variable's DEFAULT. [''] is a non-empty list, so the `or` in get_corner_wildcards() is satisfied and these two NEVER consult TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS at all -- raising that key would change nothing. The list is then filtered of the '' match-none wildcard and comes out EMPTY, no corner is matched, every violation lands in warn_violating_corner, and the step WARNS while the flow exits 0. Neither PDK ships either key, so the design configuration is the only place that can bind them. docs/34 section 8.5 recorded it; docs/36 closed it and demonstrated the gate is live by driving the checker with a synthetic violation at the slow corner. But docs/36's headline says both keys are now ['*'] in 'all three configurations that build' -- pilot_ihp, pilot_sky130 and hw/soc/pnr -- and there are FOUR. This is the fourth. trial-03-signoff ran with both at [''] and checker_audit.py calls both NO-GATE on that run tree: 'reduces to no wildcard; every corner lands in warn_violating_corner'. Added 2026-09-10. Both metrics read 0 at all three corners there, so this gates a criterion the design already meets rather than a threshold fitted to a measurement -- but 'reads 0' and 'was checked' were different statements on the run G0 cites, and that difference is the only reason these keys are here.
//hierarchy: THE SIGN-OFF RUN THIS CONFIG IS CITED FOR PREDATES THE RTL IT NOW BUILDS. trial-03-signoff ran 2026-08-25. On 2026-08-31, commit b6738e5 replicated the queue pointers, and hw/rtl/aer_fifo.v's replication defence is `keep_hierarchy` on the twelve bank instances plus the POL+MIX storage transform. Under the default flatten, yosys honours the attribute -- the log says `Keeping aer_fifo.u_wptr_a (found keep_hierarchy attribute)` nine times -- and nine $paramod submodule types survive into stat.json. librelane/steps/pyosys.py counts `every cell type whose name starts with $` as unmapped, so a PARAMETERISED USER MODULE is counted the same as a $_AND_ that failed to map: `9 Unmapped Yosys instances found` and the flow stops at Checker.YosysUnmappedCells. Nothing was unmapped -- every cell inside those nine is an sg13g2 cell. deferred_flatten synthesises hierarchically and flattens after technology mapping, which keeps the anti-merge defence through the pass that would collapse it and leaves nothing named $ behind. hw/openlane/pilot_ihp and hw/openlane/pilot_sky130 have carried this key for the same reason since before the pointers were replicated, and pilot_sky130's own comment states this failure mode verbatim; tt/src/config.json carries it too. THIS CONFIG WAS THE ONE THAT DID NOT, and the gap was invisible because nothing re-ran it: for eleven days the block's sign-off configuration could not build the block's own RTL. Added 2026-09-11. trial-03-signoff is NOT re-run and its numbers stand as recorded (docs/64); what changes is that they are now known to describe an aer_fifo WITHOUT replicated pointers.
//pdk: Both are also passed on the librelane command line by run_trial.sh. The CLI values are what the ciel wrapper uses to resolve PDK_ROOT before this file is parsed; these keys only make the config self-describing.
//util: Relative sizing at 40% target. sg13g2 has 84 cells and a single reset-flop family (docs/12 section 5), so the resizers have far less freedom than on sky130; starting loose and measuring the achieved utilization is more informative for the tile budget than forcing a die size.
//antenna: Left off deliberately, on the numbers in docs/12 section 4.5. With it off, run trial-03-signoff: 10 antenna-violating nets after global routing, 0 after detailed routing, and detailed routing's own repair inserted 3 sg13g2_antennanp cells totalling 16.33 um2. With it on, run trial-01 on the same RTL: the design finished carrying 4641 sg13g2_antennanp cells, 25261.9 um2, 11.4% of the 221386 um2 core area, for the same zero-violation result. Note that trial-01 also predates the SYNTH_PARAMETERS pin above, so this is 'the heuristic on this design' rather than a controlled A/B. The live controls are DRT_ANTENNA_REPAIR_* (3 iterations here) and GRT_ANTENNA_REPAIR_*, both left at their defaults. Do not confuse RUN_HEURISTIC_DIODE_INSERTION with GRT_REPAIR_ANTENNAS: the latter is a recognised deprecated alias for RUN_ANTENNA_REPAIR, it warns on the console and it does change behaviour, so it must not be carried over from a sky130 config by accident (docs/12 section 2.4c).
